content.doc_md:
## Tutorials

The REPEAT() function repeats a string as many times as specified.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT REPEAT("SQL Tutorial", 3);

---

REPEAT(
string
,
number
)

---

SELECT REPEAT(CustomerName, 
  2)
FROM Customers;

---

SELECT REPEAT("SQL Tutorial", 0);
```

## Tutorials

The REPLACE() function replaces all occurrences of a substring within a 
string, with a new substring.

Note:This function performs a case-sensitive 
replacement.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT REPLACE("SQL Tutorial", "SQL", "HTML");

---

REPLACE(
string
,
from_string
,
new_string
)

---

SELECT REPLACE("XYZ FGH XYZ", "X", "M");

---

SELECT REPLACE("XYZ FGH XYZ", "X", "m");

---

SELECT REPLACE("XYZ FGH XYZ", "x", "m");
```

## Tutorials

The REVERSE() function reverses a string and returns the result.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT REVERSE("SQL Tutorial");

---

REVERSE(
string
)

---

SELECT REVERSE(CustomerName)
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The RIGHT() function extracts a number of characters from a string (starting 
from right).

Tip:Also look at theLEFT()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT RIGHT("SQL Tutorial is cool", 4) AS ExtractString;

---

RIGHT(
string
,
number_of_chars
)

---

SELECT RIGHT(CustomerName, 5) AS ExtractString
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The RPAD() function right-pads a string with another string, to a certain 
length.

Note:Also look at theLPAD()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT RPAD("SQL Tutorial", 
  20, "ABC");

---

RPAD(
string
,
length
,
rpad_string
)

---

SELECT 
  RPAD(CustomerName, 30, "ABC") AS RightPadCustomerName
FROM Customers;
```
